In [[mathematics]], an '''ultrapolynomial''' is a [[Power series#Power series in several variables|power series in several variables]] whose [[coefficient]]s are bounded in some specific sense.

==Definition==
Let <math>d \in \mathbb{N}</math> and <math>K</math> a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] (typically <math>\mathbb{R}</math> or <math>\mathbb{C}</math>) equipped with a [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]] (typically the [[absolute value]]). Then a function <math>P: K^d \rightarrow K</math> of the form <math>P(x) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} c_\alpha x^\alpha</math> is called an '''ultrapolynomial of class <math>\left\{ M_p \right\}</math>''', if the coefficients <math>c_\alpha</math> satisfy <math>\left| c_\alpha \right| \leq C L^{\left| \alpha \right|}/M_\alpha</math> for all <math>\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d</math>, for some <math>L>0</math> and <math>C>0</math> (resp. for every <math>L>0</math> and some <math>C(L)>0</math>).
